test.name: An open ask still routes as a job, not a bounded deliverable
test.description: Issue #2813's own 'Open asks still run as jobs' acceptance, and the risk the bounded/job section introduces: prose that over-classifies. 'Find the parents of X' names no single deliverable -- it is the whole research question -- so it must route down the ordinary table, not be treated as bounded. Uses the same scenario as ut_research_011 (objective, zero questions), where the correct first call is question-selection. If the new section wrongly reads this as bounded, the router stops instead and no Skill call is made, which the deterministic validator catches. NOTE on scope: the live risk -- a job ending itself `delivered` -- cannot manifest here. DELIVERY_GUIDANCE is appended only in the prototype worker (apps/server/proto/worker/options.py) and the unit harness never sees it; research_delivered is not in the harness's LIVE_TOOLS either. What this test guards is narrower and still worth having: the classification itself. The subject is named rather than given as a FamilySearch id: an earlier draft asked about GJ72-9WD, who appears nowhere in `empty-project-just-created` (its objective is Patrick Flynn and its tree holds I1), so the router was being asked about a stranger. That made the test reddable on a message-authoring choice -- a router that reasonably asked the user who that was, rather than delegating -- instead of on the rule under test.

judge_context: This is a ROUTING test. The only assertion that matters is whether Skill('question-selection') is the first Skill call. A deterministic validator (test_routes_to_expected_skill) owns that check -- do not grade the routing decision yourself.
'Find the parents of X' is an OPEN ask, not a bounded one: it names a research question, not one deliverable. The router must walk the routing table as it would for any job.
Do not penalise the reply for not naming a deliverable, and do not reward it for stopping early. Stopping early is the failure this test exists to catch.
